item.title: [Translation] How Inference Works in Large Language Models
item.description:

In this article, we will break down what inference (logical reasoning) in LLMs is and see how it works. Read more

item.title: Edge Recognition is the Future of Document Processing: Smart Document Engine Weekly Digest
item.description:
Every minute counts in business. But if a document must first be sent for processing, checked, and only then its data entered into the accounting system, a gap arises between the real operation and its reflection in the system. All this time, the owner does not see the actual picture and is forced to make decisions based on outdated information. Therefore, documents need to be recognized directly where and when the operation occurs. This task is solved by edge recognition, implemented in Smart Document Engine. The platform allows processing documents directly at the point of their appearance - for example, in a warehouse or an employee's workspace - using a smartphone, tablet, or other device, and immediately transferring the ready data to corporate systems. As a result, the business gets an up-to-date picture of what's happening, and the gap between the real operation and its reflection in accounting is minimized. We've gathered the highlights of Smart Document Engine Week in one digest 👇 Read more

item.title: CMF: Millisecond Decisions Without Token Generation (Jev Alternative) With Open Weights
item.description:
Currently, the Jev model from Typesafe is widely discussed. I've decided to release my model in CMF format for personal use (License: apache-2.0), which has been operational on the gateway for a long time. How does it work? For example, a user writes that their card hasn't arrived. The application needs to select `card_arrival` and route the request to the appropriate handler, or write a Go function. Decisions must be made as quickly as possible. There are many such decision points: selecting an agent tool, determining the topic of a request, its complexity, sending a document for verification, determining task complexity and type. For these tasks, I've published CMF Decision: a model that makes decisions based on reconstruction error. The encoder, trained skills, and confidence rules are all in one `.cmf` file. New skills can be added using your own examples, and unfamiliar cases can be passed to a pluggable oracle-model that acts as a teacher. In Cortiq 0.8.0, the same file runs on CPU, Apple Metal, and Vulkan. On an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, the full local path took 1.10–1.24 ms. Below is how this mechanism works, what the results are compared to Jev and Laya, and how to run the model or add your own task. Read more

item.title: How much does an hour of a coding agent cost: a rating of five API gateways by expenses
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol have been released, and everyone has started looking at gateway prices. I've compiled prices from five gateways with payment from Russia and calculated differently: how much an hour of work in Claude Code would cost with my load – based on logs from 49 of my sessions, 138 hours of work. The spread turned out to be almost tenfold: from 181 to 1,756 rubles for the same hour on the same model. Half of the bill goes to cache writes, even though it's only 5% of incoming tokens. And the cheapest price in the table doesn't give the cheapest hour: when cache reads cost as much as regular input, an hour of agent work turns out to be almost twice as expensive as a gateway with cheap caching. Read more

item.title: Green Challenge 2026: A Physical AI Model Competition for the 'Green' Anthropomorphic Robot
item.description:
Controlling robots using images and text instructions remains a key challenge in modern robotics. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can handle many tasks, but most successes are on standard manipulators. Controlling an anthropomorphic robot like Sber's 'Green' presents a significantly higher complexity due to its many degrees of freedom, human-like hands, and mobile platform requiring whole-body coordination and balance. Sber Robotics is launching the Green Challenge competition as part of AI Journey 2026, inviting participants to develop or fine-tune control models for 'Green' to perform mobile manipulation tasks in a digital simulator. This is a complex Physical AI challenge, encompassing data preparation, multimodal perception, planning, and coordinated whole-body control.

item.title: Why DLP Doesn't Control AI and Fails to Address OWASP Top 10 for LLM, Agentic Applications, and MITRE ATLAS
item.description:
The common assertion that existing DLP solutions can prevent data leaks to AI services like ChatGPT and Copilot is technically incorrect. This article explains why DLP systems are ill-equipped to monitor AI interactions, ensure secure usage, and provide end-to-end visibility of AI within corporate infrastructure. DLP and LLM/AI Firewalls serve distinct purposes on different fronts, though both aim to prevent data leakage. Classic DLP cannot parse model dialogues, block requests before they reach LLMs, detect jailbreaks or indirect RAG injections, or manage model routing. Conversely, LLM/AI Firewalls do not replace DLP for traditional channels like email, USB drives, or printing. DLP focuses on identifying known sensitive content within established channels (email, files, removable media, web, cloud, messengers), answering the question: 'Is marked confidential data leaking through a familiar channel?'. LLM/AI Firewalls sit between the user/AI agent and the AI model, addressing different concerns. Read on.

item.title: [Translation] The DDD Paradigm Has Become Much More Important When AI Writes Code For You
item.description:
Regardless of your opinion on AI-assisted programming, software development approaches are changing. Everyone is wondering: "What will remain important?" There are as many opinions as there are people, but here's mine: most ideas from Domain-Driven Design (DDD) are now more relevant than ever, as the DDD paradigm was never limited to code itself. The more agent-based programming develops, the better we need to understand the domain, model it well, and master teamwork. Let's talk about what DDD can still teach us that AI cannot replace. The usual disclaimer: I'm writing about complex projects supported for months and years, about what teams struggle with, and where DDD shines. There's no need to use such advanced patterns in pet projects or CRUD. Read more

item.title: Agent Teams in Claude Code: From Task to Release
item.description:
Six months ago, I started building a service for myself, without a team. Agents in Claude Code write the code; I set the tasks and accept the results. Over this time, the experiment has evolved into a working system: twelve roles, a mandatory stage order, and maximum agent autonomy from task assignment to release. I'll explain who does what, how a task progresses from a backlog item to a release, and how to get started if you want to do the same.

item.title: Reaching for the Heavens: An Amateur Astronomer with an AI Agent Analyzes Euclid Telescope Data
item.description:
I was hesitant to launch Astra. Not for lack of time, but because I knew once I started, it would pull me into an abyss. You ask one question, then another, 'Can this be done?' and the model delivers something that makes it impossible to stop, with the clock showing midnight and work in the morning. So, I waited. I also wanted an idea and curiosity to ignite in my mind, something that couldn't be contained. So, when I felt it on Friday afternoon, I decided it was time. Exactly at five, I closed my work laptop, turned to my home Mac, placed my iPad with ChatGPT to the right, and a large glass of water to the left. The task ahead was not trivial. Let's even say it was crazy – we decided to programmatically access the data from Euclid, the new telescope hanging a million and a half kilometers from Earth at the L2 Lagrange point, and process its data through a new GPT 6 model – Astra Extra High, and... That 'and' was the main question. Read more

item.title: The Junior Was Given an AI, and the Senior Got More Work
item.description:
With an AI assistant, a junior's work looks as neat as a senior's, and you can no longer find mistakes by appearance. If the author cannot explain how they got the result, the reviewer reconstructs the path themselves and essentially does the task a second time. I analyze where the senior's time is burned out, using an nginx fix as an example, and what requirements for submitting work can fix this. Read more →

item.title: Sixteen promises and two models that tried to break them: how we released skillmem 0.12
item.description:
In 0.11 we ran AI reviewers over code for forty rounds and found many bugs. But each reviewer had their own idea of what "correct" means. In 0.12 we started from the other end: we wrote down sixteen invariants that our MCP memory promises, and then two models from different labs spent ten days looking for counterexamples. Only findings with reproduction were counted. I'll tell you what they broke (Windows counted NUL as a terminal), what it cost, and what we consciously left in Known issues. Read on

item.title: AI model hallucinations in code usually break the build. With a fabricated package, it's different: its name can be taken by a malicious actor
item.description:
I took 139 package names that five recent AI models hallucinate identically and checked each against live PyPI and npm on September 22. These are registries from which libraries for Python and JavaScript are installed. The list is valuable because it's not tied to a single neural network: if all five hallucinate the same name, users of any of them are at risk. The list was disclosed on April 30, 2026. 7 out of 139 names are taken. Under one of them, metro-evaluator, malicious code was found in December 2025: npm removed it five days later and replaced it with a placeholder. This was before the list was disclosed, and whether it was a coincidence or a calculated move for a hallucinated name is not visible from the registry. The other six names are occupied by four existing third-party projects, a brand owner's placeholder, and an empty 53-byte package that appeared after the list's disclosure. Following an AI's advice, 'pip install odf' will install someone else's tool instead of the intended library. Read more
